# Objective

This analysis assesses socioeconomic inequalities in three smoking outcomes:

1. Daily smoking
2. Current smoking
3. Ever smoking

Daily smoking intensity is excluded from Objective 2 because of substantial missingness. Socioeconomic position is represented by education, household income, employment status, and occupational class. Subjective income feeling is treated as an adjustment covariate, not as a socioeconomic exposure.

For each smoking outcome, unadjusted and sequentially adjusted multilevel Poisson regression models are fitted to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs). Models include a random intercept for country and use the analysis weight `anweight`.

```{r load-packages}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(forcats)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)

library(glmmTMB)

library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Load Data

```{r load-data}
data_path <- dplyr::case_when(
  file.exists("ess_clean.rds") ~ "ess_clean.rds",
  file.exists("../ess_clean.rds") ~ "../ess_clean.rds",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)

if (is.na(data_path)) {
  stop("Could not find ess_clean.rds in the working directory or parent directory.")
}

ess_clean <- readRDS(data_path)

cat("Data loaded successfully.\n")
cat("Sample size:", nrow(ess_clean), "respondents\n")
cat("Variables:", ncol(ess_clean), "\n")
```

# Prepare Analysis Data

Reference groups are set so that higher socioeconomic position is the comparison category for each SES marker. For covariates, the first factor level is the reference category.

```{r prepare-data}
ess_ml_data <- ess_clean %>%
  mutate(
    Daily_smoker = as.numeric(Daily_smoker),
    current_smoking = as.numeric(current_smoking),
    ever_smoking = as.numeric(ever_smoking),

    survey_year = factor(survey_year, levels = c("2014", "2023")),
    cntry = factor(cntry),

    education = factor(education, levels = c("High", "Medium", "Low")),
    income_group = factor(income_group, levels = c("High", "Middle", "Low")),
    employment = factor(
      employment,
      levels = c("Employed", "Inactive (other)", "Retired", "Unemployed")
    ),
    occupation = factor(
      occupation,
      levels = c("Non-manual (higher)", "Non-manual (lower)", "Manual")
    ),

    income_feeling = factor(
      income_feeling,
      levels = c("Living comfortably", "Coping", "Difficult / very difficult")
    ),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("Male", "Female")),
    marital = factor(
      marital,
      levels = c("Married/Civil union", "Never married", "Separated/Divorced", "Widowed")
    ),
    agea = as.numeric(agea),
    anweight = as.numeric(anweight)
  )
```

# Modelling Functions

```{r model-functions}
fit_ml_poisson <- function(data, outcome, formula_rhs, needed_vars) {
  model_vars <- unique(c(outcome, needed_vars, "cntry", "anweight"))

  model_data <- data %>%
    filter(if_all(all_of(model_vars), ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
    filter(anweight > 0)

  if (nrow(model_data) == 0 || n_distinct(model_data[[outcome]]) < 2) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  model_formula <- as.formula(
    paste0(outcome, " ~ ", formula_rhs, " + (1 | cntry)")
  )

  tryCatch(
    glmmTMB(
      formula = model_formula,
      family = poisson(link = "log"),
      weights = anweight,
      data = model_data,
      REML = FALSE
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      warning(
        "Model failed for: ", outcome, " ~ ", formula_rhs,
        "\nError: ", conditionMessage(e)
      )
      NULL
    }
  )
}

tidy_ml_poisson <- function(fit, outcome_label, model_type, model_label) {
  if (is.null(fit)) {
    return(tibble())
  }

  tidy(
    fit,
    effects = "fixed",
    conf.int = TRUE,
    conf.method = "wald",
    exponentiate = TRUE
  ) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    transmute(
      Outcome = outcome_label,
      model_type = model_type,
      model_label = model_label,
      term_raw = term,
      PR = estimate,
      CI_low = conf.low,
      CI_high = conf.high,
      p_value = p.value
    )
}

decode_terms <- function(results) {
  results %>%
    mutate(
      Variable = case_when(
        str_detect(term_raw, "^education") ~ "Education level",
        str_detect(term_raw, "^income_group") ~ "Household income",
        str_detect(term_raw, "^employment") ~ "Employment status",
        str_detect(term_raw, "^occupation") ~ "Occupational class",
        str_detect(term_raw, "^income_feeling") ~ "Subjective income feeling",
        term_raw == "agea" ~ "Age",
        str_detect(term_raw, "^sex") ~ "Sex",
        str_detect(term_raw, "^marital") ~ "Marital status",
        str_detect(term_raw, "^survey_year") ~ "Survey year",
        TRUE ~ term_raw
      ),
      Level = case_when(
        str_detect(term_raw, "^education") ~ str_remove(term_raw, "^education"),
        str_detect(term_raw, "^income_group") ~ str_remove(term_raw, "^income_group"),
        str_detect(term_raw, "^employment") ~ str_remove(term_raw, "^employment"),
        str_detect(term_raw, "^occupation") ~ str_remove(term_raw, "^occupation"),
        str_detect(term_raw, "^income_feeling") ~ str_remove(term_raw, "^income_feeling"),
        term_raw == "agea" ~ "Per one-year increase",
        str_detect(term_raw, "^sex") ~ str_remove(term_raw, "^sex"),
        str_detect(term_raw, "^marital") ~ str_remove(term_raw, "^marital"),
        str_detect(term_raw, "^survey_year") ~ str_remove(term_raw, "^survey_year"),
        TRUE ~ term_raw
      ),
      PR_CI = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", PR, CI_low, CI_high),
      p_fmt = case_when(
        is.na(p_value) ~ NA_character_,
        p_value < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p_value)
      )
    )
}

keep_exposure_terms <- function(results) {
  results %>%
    decode_terms() %>%
    filter(
      case_when(
        Variable == "Education level" ~ exposure_var == "education",
        Variable == "Household income" ~ exposure_var == "income_group",
        Variable == "Employment status" ~ exposure_var == "employment",
        Variable == "Occupational class" ~ exposure_var == "occupation",
        TRUE ~ FALSE
      )
    )
}
```

# Unadjusted Models

Each unadjusted model includes one SES marker and a country-level random intercept.

```{r unadjusted-models}
obj2_upr_results <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  obj2_outcomes,
  obj2_ses
) %>%
  pmap_dfr(function(outcome, outcome_label, var, label, reference) {
    data_tmp <- ess_ml_data %>%
      mutate("{var}" := fct_relevel(factor(.data[[var]]), reference))

    fit <- fit_ml_poisson(
      data = data_tmp,
      outcome = outcome,
      formula_rhs = var,
      needed_vars = var
    )

    tidy_ml_poisson(
      fit = fit,
      outcome_label = outcome_label,
      model_type = "UPR",
      model_label = label
    ) %>%
      mutate(
        exposure_label = label,
        exposure_var = var,
        exposure_type = "SES",
        .after = model_label
      )
  })

cat("Unadjusted models completed.\n")
cat("Unadjusted PR estimates:", nrow(obj2_upr_results), "\n")
```

# Sequential Adjusted Models

Three models are fitted for each outcome and SES marker:

- Model 1: SES marker only
- Model 2: SES marker + age + sex + marital status + subjective income feeling
- Model 3: Model 2 + survey year

```{r define-sequential-models}
sequential_models <- tribble(
  ~model_num, ~model_name, ~formula_components,
  1, "M1: SES only", "ses_var",
  2, "M2: SES + covariates", "ses_var + agea + sex + marital + income_feeling",
  3, "M3: SES + covariates + survey year", "ses_var + agea + sex + marital + income_feeling + survey_year"
)

sequential_models
```

```{r sequential-models}
obj2_sequential_fits <- list()
obj2_sequential_results_list <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(obj2_outcomes))) {
  outcome <- obj2_outcomes$outcome[i]
  outcome_label <- obj2_outcomes$outcome_label[i]

  cat("Processing outcome:", outcome_label, "\n")

  outcome_results <- pmap_dfr(
    obj2_ses,
    function(var, label, reference) {
      data_tmp <- ess_ml_data %>%
        mutate("{var}" := fct_relevel(factor(.data[[var]]), reference))

      fits_list <- map(
        seq_len(nrow(sequential_models)),
        function(m) {
          formula_rhs <- str_replace(
            sequential_models$formula_components[m],
            "ses_var",
            var
          )
          needed_vars <- str_split(formula_rhs, " \\+ ")[[1]]

          fit_ml_poisson(
            data = data_tmp,
            outcome = outcome,
            formula_rhs = formula_rhs,
            needed_vars = needed_vars
          )
        }
      )

      key <- paste(outcome, var, sep = "_")
      obj2_sequential_fits[[key]] <<- list(
        outcome = outcome,
        outcome_label = outcome_label,
        exposure_var = var,
        exposure_label = label,
        exposure_type = "SES",
        reference = reference,
        fits = fits_list
      )

      pmap_dfr(
        tibble(model_num = sequential_models$model_num, fit = fits_list),
        function(model_num, fit) {
          tidy_ml_poisson(
            fit = fit,
            outcome_label = outcome_label,
            model_type = "Sequential",
            model_label = sequential_models$model_name[model_num]
          ) %>%
            mutate(
              exposure_label = label,
              exposure_var = var,
              exposure_type = "SES",
              model_num = model_num
            )
        }
      )
    }
  )

  obj2_sequential_results_list[[i]] <- outcome_results
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

obj2_sequential_results <- bind_rows(obj2_sequential_results_list)

cat("Sequential models completed.\n")
cat("Estimates extracted:", nrow(obj2_sequential_results), "\n")
cat("Outcome-SES combinations stored:", length(obj2_sequential_fits), "\n")
```

# Model Comparison

AIC and BIC are compared across sequential models for each outcome and SES marker. The final adjusted table uses the lowest-AIC model. BIC is retained as a secondary model-comparison statistic.

```{r model-comparison}
model_comparison_results <- map_dfr(
  obj2_sequential_fits,
  function(entry) {
    tibble(
      Outcome = entry$outcome_label,
      SES_model = entry$exposure_label,
      SES_variable = entry$exposure_var,
      Model = sequential_models$model_name,
      Model_num = sequential_models$model_num,
      AIC = map_dbl(entry$fits, ~ if (is.null(.x)) NA_real_ else AIC(.x)),
      BIC = map_dbl(entry$fits, ~ if (is.null(.x)) NA_real_ else BIC(.x)),
      LogLik = map_dbl(entry$fits, ~ if (is.null(.x)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(logLik(.x)))
    ) %>%
      filter(!is.na(AIC)) %>%
      mutate(
        Delta_AIC = AIC - min(AIC, na.rm = TRUE),
        Delta_BIC = BIC - min(BIC, na.rm = TRUE),
        Best_AIC = Delta_AIC == 0,
        Best_BIC = Delta_BIC == 0
      )
  }
)

model_comparison_results %>%
  select(Outcome, SES_model, Model, AIC, BIC, Delta_AIC, Delta_BIC) %>%
  arrange(Outcome, SES_model, Delta_AIC)
```

```{r best-models}
best_models <- model_comparison_results %>%
  group_by(Outcome, SES_model, SES_variable) %>%
  filter(Delta_AIC == min(Delta_AIC, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(
    Outcome,
    SES_model,
    SES_variable,
    Model,
    Model_num,
    AIC,
    BIC,
    Delta_AIC,
    Delta_BIC
  )

best_models %>%
  arrange(Outcome, SES_model) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# Final Adjusted Results

```{r extract-final-results}
obj2_final_results <- pmap_dfr(
  best_models,
  function(Outcome, SES_model, SES_variable, Model, Model_num, ...) {
    outcome_var <- obj2_outcomes %>%
      filter(outcome_label == Outcome) %>%
      pull(outcome) %>%
      first()

    ses_reference <- obj2_ses %>%
      filter(var == SES_variable) %>%
      pull(reference) %>%
      first()

    formula_rhs <- str_replace(
      sequential_models$formula_components[Model_num],
      "ses_var",
      SES_variable
    )
    needed_vars <- str_split(formula_rhs, " \\+ ")[[1]]

    data_tmp <- ess_ml_data %>%
      mutate(
        "{SES_variable}" := fct_relevel(
          factor(.data[[SES_variable]]),
          ses_reference
        )
      )

    fit <- fit_ml_poisson(
      data = data_tmp,
      outcome = outcome_var,
      formula_rhs = formula_rhs,
      needed_vars = needed_vars
    )

    tidy_ml_poisson(
      fit = fit,
      outcome_label = Outcome,
      model_type = "APR",
      model_label = SES_model
    ) %>%
      mutate(
        exposure_label = SES_model,
        exposure_var = SES_variable,
        exposure_type = "SES",
        selected_model = Model,
        selected_model_num = Model_num
      )
  }
)

cat("Final adjusted model results extracted.\n")
cat("Adjusted PR estimates:", nrow(obj2_final_results), "\n")
```

# Results Table

Only SES exposure terms are shown in the main results table. Age, sex, marital status, subjective income feeling, and survey year are adjustment variables where included by the selected model.

```{r build-results-table}
obj2_upr_decoded <- obj2_upr_results %>%
  keep_exposure_terms()

obj2_final_decoded <- obj2_final_results %>%
  keep_exposure_terms()

upr_wide <- obj2_upr_decoded %>%
  select(Outcome, Variable, Level, PR_CI, p_fmt) %>%
  rename(
    `UPR (95% CI)` = PR_CI,
    `UPR p-value` = p_fmt
  )

apr_wide <- obj2_final_decoded %>%
  select(Outcome, model_label, Variable, Level, PR_CI, p_fmt, selected_model) %>%
  rename(
    `SES Model` = model_label,
    `APR (95% CI)` = PR_CI,
    `APR p-value` = p_fmt,
    `Selected model` = selected_model
  )

obj2_combined_table <- apr_wide %>%
  left_join(
    upr_wide,
    by = c("Outcome", "Variable", "Level")
  ) %>%
  select(
    Outcome,
    `SES Model`,
    Variable,
    Level,
    `UPR (95% CI)`,
    `UPR p-value`,
    `APR (95% CI)`,
    `APR p-value`,
    `Selected model`
  )

reference_rows <- crossing(
  Outcome = obj2_outcomes$outcome_label,
  obj2_ses
) %>%
  transmute(
    Outcome = Outcome,
    `SES Model` = label,
    Variable = label,
    Level = reference,
    `UPR (95% CI)` = "1.00 (Reference)",
    `UPR p-value` = "-",
    `APR (95% CI)` = "1.00 (Reference)",
    `APR p-value` = "-",
    `Selected model` = NA_character_
  )

obj2_final_table <- bind_rows(reference_rows, obj2_combined_table) %>%
  mutate(
    Outcome = factor(
      Outcome,
      levels = obj2_outcomes$outcome_label
    ),
    Variable = factor(
      Variable,
      levels = obj2_ses$label
    ),
    level_order = case_when(
      Variable == "Education level" & Level == "High" ~ 1,
      Variable == "Education level" & Level == "Medium" ~ 2,
      Variable == "Education level" & Level == "Low" ~ 3,
      Variable == "Household income" & Level == "High" ~ 1,
      Variable == "Household income" & Level == "Middle" ~ 2,
      Variable == "Household income" & Level == "Low" ~ 3,
      Variable == "Employment status" & Level == "Employed" ~ 1,
      Variable == "Employment status" & Level == "Inactive (other)" ~ 2,
      Variable == "Employment status" & Level == "Retired" ~ 3,
      Variable == "Employment status" & Level == "Unemployed" ~ 4,
      Variable == "Occupational class" & Level == "Non-manual (higher)" ~ 1,
      Variable == "Occupational class" & Level == "Non-manual (lower)" ~ 2,
      Variable == "Occupational class" & Level == "Manual" ~ 3,
      TRUE ~ 99
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(Outcome, Variable, level_order) %>%
  select(-level_order) %>%
  group_by(Outcome, `SES Model`) %>%
  mutate(`SES Model` = if_else(row_number() == 1, as.character(`SES Model`), "")) %>%
  ungroup()

obj2_final_table
```

# Optional Sensitivity Analysis: Survey Year Interactions

Use this section if the study needs to test whether socioeconomic inequalities changed between 2014 and 2023.

```{r survey-year-interactions, eval=FALSE}
interaction_results <- pmap_dfr(
  crossing(obj2_outcomes, obj2_ses),
  function(outcome, outcome_label, var, label, reference) {
    data_tmp <- ess_ml_data %>%
      mutate("{var}" := fct_relevel(factor(.data[[var]]), reference))

    formula_rhs <- paste0(
      var,
      " * survey_year + agea + sex + marital + income_feeling"
    )
    needed_vars <- c(var, "survey_year", "agea", "sex", "marital", "income_feeling")

    fit <- fit_ml_poisson(
      data = data_tmp,
      outcome = outcome,
      formula_rhs = formula_rhs,
      needed_vars = needed_vars
    )

    tidy_ml_poisson(
      fit = fit,
      outcome_label = outcome_label,
      model_type = "Interaction",
      model_label = label
    ) %>%
      filter(str_detect(term_raw, ":")) %>%
      mutate(
        exposure_label = label,
        exposure_var = var
      )
  }
)

interaction_results
```
